ground_truth.unit: SD of PISA math score per SD of national patience
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("National Preferences and Student Achievement across Countries: The Intertwined Roles of Patience and Risk-taking"), column (3), row Patience.  Student-level least squares regression of the PISA math test score (original PISA scores divided by 100, so a unit is one standard deviation), pooled over all PISA waves 2000-2018, on the country's Global Preference Survey patience and risk-taking entered together.  Each preference is z-standardised in the analytical sample and collapsed to the country level. Controls: student gender, age and migration status, imputation dummies, and test-wave fixed effects.  Weighted by students' sampling probabilities within countries, giving equal weight to each country.  Sample: all students in the 49 PISA countries with GPS data.  Robust standard errors clustered at the country level.

ground_truth.context: Table 1, column (3), row Risk-taking.  Same regression as table1_col3_patience (patience and risk-taking entered together).

ground_truth.unit: SD of PISA math score per SD of country-of-origin patience
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Patience, Risk-taking, and Student Achievement: Migrant Analysis"), column (3), row Patience (country-of-origin). Least squares regression of the PISA math score (divided by 100), PISA waves 2003-2018, on the GPS patience and risk-taking of the student's country of origin, entered together.  Sample: migrant students, both of whose parents were born outside the country where the student attends school, with an identified origin country that has GPS data.  First-generation migrants are assigned their country of birth, second-generation migrants their father's country of origin.  The sample spans 58 countries of origin and 48 residence countries.  Includes the 180 residence- country-by-wave fixed effects.  Controls: student gender, age, a dummy for an OECD country of origin, and imputation dummies. Robust standard errors clustered at the country-of-origin level.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Full PISA file pisa_full_gps_final.dta (1,992,276 rows, 2.5 GB) cannot be read through the mount within the 300 s sandbox limit (~5-10 MB/s; a full CSV fread and a full chunked read both timed out in exploration). Table 1 is estimated on a systematic 50% subsample: 3000-row blocks every 6000 rows (all 333 blocks read; every country hit, 49 countries, 253 of the country-waves), read with haven::read_dta(col_select, skip, n_max) so only needed columns are kept. wgtc weights are renormalised within country-wave so every country keeps equal total weight and equal weight per wave.

table1_col3_observations = full-file row count (from the .dta header) times the complete-case share of loaded rows; exploratory reads of all 1,992,276 rows (attempts 5 and 6) found no missing values in any regression variable.

The data contain only raw country-level GPS means for residence countries. The paper's individual-level z-standardisation in the 49-country sample is reconstructed as SD = sqrt(mean within-country GPS variance + variance of country means), with within-country SDs from patience_sd/risktaking_sd in the migrant file (43 of 49 countries matched; others get the mean within variance). Validated on the 58 origin countries, where it reproduces the migrant file's own coo_patience/coo_risktaking standardisation slope to <1%.

Table 2 uses the migrant file's already-standardised coo_* preferences, residence country-by-wave fixed effects, weights wgt (the student sampling weight in that file), controls female, age, coo_oecd, imfemale, image, SEs clustered by country of origin. A singleton country-wave observation is kept (fixef.rm = none; coefficients unaffected).

Table 1 controls: female, age, migra1, migra2 (migration status, mean-imputed where missing), imputation dummies imfemale, image, immigra0, wave fixed effects; SEs clustered by country. Natives (col 5) = students with observed native status (migra0 == 1 and immigra0 == 0); students with imputed migration status are excluded from the natives subsample. image is dropped as collinear in the 50% subsample (no imputed ages loaded).
deviations_stdout: full PISA file (1992276 rows, 2.5 GB) cannot be read through the mount within the 300 s sandbox limit (~10 MB/s); Table 1 is estimated on a systematic subsample of 996276 rows (50.0%): 3000-row blocks every 6000 rows, 333 of 333 blocks read; only the needed columns are loaded (haven col_select); sampling weights wgtc are renormalised within country-wave so each country keeps equal total weight and equal weight per wave.
table1_col3_observations is the full-file row count times the complete-case share of the loaded rows (no missing values were found in any regression variable in exploratory reads of all rows).

the data hold only country-level GPS means; the individual-level z-standardisation in the 49-country sample is reconstructed with the within-country GPS SDs of the migrant file (validated on the 58 origin countries, where it reproduces the file's own standardisation slope to <1%).
cell.notes: Blind independent reproduction in R (haven + data.table + fixest). Attempts 1-6 were exploratory (no RESULT lines): attempt-1 full CSV fread timed out (killed at 300 s, recorded 124); 2-6 measured mount throughput, checked variable semantics (wgtc = country-equalised weight, raw country GPS values, migra coding), validated the SD reconstruction, and checked missingness over all rows; attempt-4 crashed on a header-print bug after printing its diagnostics. Attempt-7 was the first scored run and crashed on a ReadStat block-read error; fixed with tryCatch/retry, fixef.rm = none, invisible(gc()). Attempts 8 and 9 ran the identical repaired script but hung/failed during a Docker daemon wedge (docker exit 125, 'containers/<id>/start: EOF'); R never started. Per the coordinator these are not real attempts and are recorded with kind "" (their feedback.txt explains). The final run is the same script re-run after Docker was restarted; a sibling cell was reading the same mount concurrently, but all 333 blocks still loaded before the deadline. Paper values were never consulted; reading the paper's method sections exposed some non-withheld Table 1/2 cells, and nothing was tuned toward them.
